summary: Design agent completed Low-Level Design for NFR-SEC-002 (Issue #31) — Enforce Content Security Policy headers; eliminate inline scripts and eval(). LLD covers: production CSP header value (default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; worker-src blob:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests), nginx.conf security headers block (CSP + X-Content-Type-Options + X-Frame-Options + Referrer-Policy + Permissions-Policy), ESLint rule additions (no-eval, no-new-func, no-script-url, no-implied-eval), dev-only Vite cspNoncePlugin interface (apply: 'serve', transformIndexHtml nonce injection), CspNonce module (getCspNonce + applyNonce, dev-only), 4 sequence diagrams (production request flow, CSP violation detection E2E, build-time ESLint enforcement, dev server nonce flow), threat model (8 threats + mitigations), 5 test case mappings (T-SEC-002-01 through T-SEC-002-05), 5 open questions, and implementation checklist. Draft PR #50 is open on branch feature/31-nfr-sec-002-design awaiting Gate 6a human design review. Area determined as frontend (pure client-side SPA).

[HIGH] Verify Open Question #3: Does Three.js use eval() internally? If yes, unsafe-eval must be added to script-src, significantly weakening the CSP.
[HIGH] Verify Open Question #4: Does the Vite production build inject any inline scripts into index.html? If yes, a nonce or hash must be added to script-src.
[MEDIUM] Decide on Open Question #1: Can style-src 'unsafe-inline' be eliminated? Requires auditing all Tailwind + Three.js style mutations.
[LOW] Decide on Open Question #2: Should a CSP report-to endpoint be added for violation observability?
[LOW] Confirm Open Question #5: Is upgrade-insecure-requests safe for local Docker HTTP development?
